'''Francesco Petruccione''' is an Italian born South African physicist serving as a [[professor]] of [[Physics]] at [[Stellenbosch University]] and the director of the [[National Institute for Theoretical and Computational Sciences]] (NITheCS).<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Mathe |first=Mthokozisi S'thembiso |date=2021-06-24 |title=Francesco Petruccione - |url=https://scp.ukzn.ac.za/francesco-petruccione/ |access-date=2022-12-29 |website=School of Chemistry & Physics |language=en-ZA |archive-date=2022-12-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221229011416/https://scp.ukzn.ac.za/francesco-petruccione/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=News - Top quantum scientist joins SU's School for... |url=https://www.sun.ac.za/english/Lists/news/DispForm.aspx?ID=9203 |access-date=2022-12-29 |website=www.sun.ac.za}}</ref> With a wealth of experience in his field, he previously held the position of [[professor]] and [[Pro Vice-Chancellor]] of [[Big Data]] and [[Informatics]] at the [[University of KwaZulu-Natal]] (UKZN). Petruccione is also a member of the [[Academy of Science of South Africa]] and a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of South Africa]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Francesco Petruccione {{!}} The AAS |url=https://www.aasciences.africa/fellow/francesco-petruccione |access-date=2022-12-29 |website=www.aasciences.africa |archive-date=2022-12-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221229001550/https://www.aasciences.africa/fellow/francesco-petruccione }}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Prof. F. Petruccione — Centre for Quantum Technology |url=https://quantum.ukzn.ac.za/prof-f-petruccione/ |access-date=2022-12-29 |website=Quantum Research Group UKZN |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==

Francesco Petruccione was born in [[Genoa]], [[Italy]], in 1961.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Petruccione |url=https://africanscientists.africa/business-directory/petruccione/ |access-date=2022-12-29 |website=African Scientists Directory |language=en-US}}</ref> He pursued his [[undergraduate]] studies in [[physics]] at the [[University of Freiburg]], [[Germany]], where he earned his first degree in the field. Petruccione continued his academic journey at the same institution, earning his [[doctorate]] in 1988 and his [[Habilitation]] degree (Dr. rer. nat. habil.) in 1994.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Francesco Petruccione - GESDA Science Breakthrough Radar |url=https://radar.gesda.global/* |access-date=2022-12-29 |website=radar.gesda.global |language=en |archive-date=2022-05-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220516054659/https://radar.gesda.global/ }}</ref>

== Career ==

In 2004, he became a professor of Theoretical Physics at the [[University of KwaZulu-Natal]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof Francesco Petruccione |url=http://worldscienceforum.org/participants/petruccione-francesco-52956 |access-date=2022-12-29 |website=World Science Forum |archive-date=2022-12-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221229002349/https://worldscienceforum.org/participants/petruccione-francesco-52956 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and was awarded an Innovation Fund grant the following year to establish a Centre for Quantum Technology. Petruccione went on to hold the position of South African Research Chair for [[Quantum]] [[Information Processing]] and [[Communication]] Technology in 2007.<ref name=":2" />

In addition to his role as [[interim director]] of the [[National Institute for Theoretical and Computational Science]] (NITheCS), Petruccione also held an [[adjunct professor]] position at the Korean Advanced Institute for Science and Technology. In 2018, he was appointed [[Pro Vice-Chancellor]] of [[Big Data]] and [[Informatics]] at the [[University of KwaZulu-Natal]] (UKZN) before moving to [[Stellenbosch University]] in 2022 as a professor of [[Physics]] and [[Quantum Computing]] as part of the Physics Department and the School of Data Science and Computational Thinking.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Aimee |date=2022-06-03 |title=Top quantum scientist joins Stellenbosch University |url=https://nithecs.ac.za/top-quantum-scientist-joins-stellenbosch-university/ |access-date=2022-12-29 |website=NITheCS |language=en-ZA}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Staff |url=https://nithecs.ac.za/staff/ |access-date=2022-12-29 |website=NITheCS |language=en-ZA}}</ref><ref name=":3" /><ref name=":4" />
[[File:Francesco knighting ceremony.png|thumb|455x455px|Francesco Petruccione receiving recognition at the Italian Order of the Star ceremony|center]]
In 2023 Petruccione was honored with the title of [[Cavaliere]] della Stella d'Italia, [[Order of the Star of Italy]], at a function at the Italian Embassy in Cape Town, South Africa.<ref>{{Cite web |last=RW-Admin |date=2023-06-08 |title=SU quantum expert receives Italian knighthood {{!}} Stellenbosch University |url=https://www.su.ac.za/en/node/6937 |access-date=2026-04-30 |website=www.su.ac.za |language=en}}</ref> As of May 2024 he has officially been appointed as director of NITheCS.

In 2025, he was involved in an international collaboration with the University of Science and Technology of China, where he contributed to a record-breaking intercontinental satellite-based quantum key distribution (QKD) link between South Africa and China.<ref>{{cite web
 |title=South Africa and China establish record-breaking 12,900 km ultra-secure quantum satellite link
 |url=https://www.su.ac.za/en/node/19887
 |website=Stellenbosch University
 |date=19 March 2025
 |access-date=30 April 2026
}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal
 |last1=Li
 |first1=Y.
 |title=Microsatellite-based real-time quantum key distribution
 |journal=Nature
 |year=2025
 |doi=10.1038/s41586-025-08739-z
 |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-025-08739-z
 |access-date=30 April 2026
 |arxiv=2408.10994
 }}</ref>
